text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: p99 latency breach for customer Equinox (VPC dedicated pool eu2). Auto-page to oncall-sre.
oncall-sre: I got the page, taking lead.
maya: I'm on metrics + tracing. pulling p95/p99 now.
leo: Support thread opened with Equinox CSM (elena). they report degraded response times in their staging/production routes.
jen: I'm looping in account operations and will message legal if needed.
sam-infra: Checking pool capacity and GPU utilization.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-5843219876; severity=P1; runbook=dedicated-latency.
maya: Quick snapshot: baseline p95 ~ 120ms; current p95 ~ 460ms; p99 jumping to ~2100ms for eu2-dedicated. error rate not elevated (~0.1% 5xx).
oncall-sre: Any recent deploys to that pool?
sam-infra: No deploys in last 2 hours. autoscaler shows no new nodes added; pool at 98% GPU memory and 95% compute.
maya: Traces point to long tail during KV cache misses and a heavy attention kernel hot path. Hotspot tied to requests from tenant equinox-prod-01.
elena-equinox: Confirming increased latency on our end after 09:12 UTC. Impacting interactive search flows (users complaining). No spikes in request volume from our side.
leo: Can you share a few request ids? helps tracing.
elena-equinox: Sent three IDs in DM.
oncall-sre: Quick mitigation options: 1) throttle Equinox tenant to mitigate noisy neighbor 2) move Equinox to warm spare region (eu1) 3) evict long-running sessions 4) add burst capacity.
maya: My recommendation: immediate tenant isolation + evict stale sessions, then scale burst if isolation not enough. isolation buys time non-disruptively.
sam-infra: I can apply tenant-level egress throttle and start scale-up (burst nodes) but scale-up ETA ~5-7 minutes to be ready.
oncall-sre: Do isolation now. sam, apply throttle at 50% of their concurrent requests, mark for monitoring.
sam-infra: Running action: `redwoodctl tenant throttle --tenant equinox-prod-01 --region eu2 --concurrency 0.5`
ops-bot: Action accepted: throttle command queued to agent pool.
(30s)
ops-bot: Command output: OK - throttle applied.
maya: After throttle: p95 -> 210ms, p99 -> 900ms. CPU and GPU pressure down to 82%/75%.
oncall-sre: Good, visible improvement. Notify Equinox about mitigation.
leo: @elena-equinox we've applied a temporary throttle to reduce tail latency while we investigate. Expected recovery to ~p95 250-300ms. Monitoring closely.
elena-equinox: Acknowledged. Please avoid full cutover / migration unless necessary.
jen: Noted — will keep customer informed. Do we have root cause hypothesis?
maya: Hypothesis: a tail of large-context requests triggered repeated KV cache misses and pushed attention kernel into a slow path on our quantized code path under specific sequence lengths. It appears workload shape from equinox has changed (longer sessions).
oncall-sre: Can we mitigate at platform level? suggestions: enable aggressive prefix caching for that tenant, increase per-tenant KV cache allocation, or offload large-context requests to a compatible variant with larger KV capacity.
sam-infra: I can toggle prefix caching TTL and bump tenant KV cache quota. doing `redwoodctl tenant config set equinox-prod-01 --kv-cache-quota 2x --prefix-ttl 60s`
ops-bot: Command queued.
(90s)
ops-bot: Config update applied: KV cache quota increased, prefix TTL set to 60s.
maya: After cache bump: p95 ~ 170ms, p99 ~ 540ms. significant improvement but still above baseline p99.
oncall-sre: Next step: consider model variant fallback for heavy requests — route traffic for >2k token requests to variant with optimized attention kernels (quantized L4).
sam-infra: We have warm variant in eu1 and eu2 compatible with routing. Initiating canary redirect for large-context requests from Equinox to variant-v2.
oncall-sre: Start small canary (5%).
ops-bot: Canary route created: equinox-prod-01 large-context -> variant-v2 (5%).
maya: Canary shows p99 ~ 260ms for the routed requests. Positive signal.
elena-equinox: Is there any user-visible change for routed requests? any API differences?
leo: No API change; same response schema. slight latency improvement for those heavy calls.
oncall-sre: Plan: keep throttle + cache bump + canary routing. Monitor for 15 minutes. If stable, promote 50% and then 100%, or scale pool.
jen: I'll draft a short status update to Equinox: "Temporary throttle and cache adjustments applied; canary routing for large-context requests shows improvement; engineering monitoring closely."
elena-equinox: Thanks — please include ETA for full resolution.
oncall-sre: ETA: if canary remains stable, we can promote in ~20-30m and expect p99 back near baseline. If canary fails, prepare for region failover to eu1 warm spare (~10-15m to warm traffic).
maya: Captured logs and traces for RCA. I'll open a follow-up ticket for codepath optimization and quantization parameter tuning tied to equinox workload.
sam-infra: Scaling remains available if needed. I can add two burst nodes now (ETA 6m).
oncall-sre: Hold on additional scaling for now, prefer promoting variant if canary good. avoids adding cost.
(8m)
ops-bot: Monitoring alert: p99 trending downward to 420ms across pool.
maya: Marking incident as "mitigated" for now but keeping call open for observation window.
leo: Notifying Equinox: mitigation in place, latency improving, will provide follow-up RCA.
elena-equinox: Appreciate the quick actions. Please escalate if anything changes.
oncall-sre: Thanks team. Post-incident actions: - RCA ticket (maya) - Quant kernel tuning (research) - Improve runbook steps for tenant isolation and canary routing (oncall-sre) - Customer postmortem and credit evaluation (jen/leo).
jen: I'll coordinate customer postmortem and timeline.
ops-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident closed when stable for 1h.
maya: Dropping traces/links to the incident folder in case needed: `s3://redwood-incidents/5843219876/traces.tar.gz`
leo: Thanks everyone. Closing updates will follow once 1h stable window passes. :white_check_mark:
